navaid.name: TEN POUND ISLAND LIGHT
navaid.description: The Ten Pound Island Light possesses Integrity of location, design, setting, materials and workmanship. It is a well preserved example of the cast iron towers of the period; it remains an important location in the navigation of Gloucester Harbor.

Ruins of one of two boat launch rail systems in use in 1934. It is unclear from the aerial photo weather launch rail served the Lighthouse, the Coast Guard Air Station or the Fish Hatchery.
Boathouse and launching rails of the former Dolliver's Neck Coast Guard Station. The Coast Guard Station relocated to its current site in 1974.
